target.title: perf: cache Claude CLI version probes by executable fingerprint
target.body:
### Description
Claude OAuth usage refresh currently executes `claude --version` while constructing every request User-Agent. This PR introduces a thread-safe, memory-resident cache that keys on the resolved executable's fingerprint (path, modification date, file size, and inode) to avoid spawning unnecessary PTY/CLI subprocesses (which can happen up to 288 times/day on default settings).

### Changes
- Added `ClaudeExecutableFingerprint` and `PendingDetection` to `ProviderVersionDetector`.
- Implemented thread-safe caching and single-flight coalescing for concurrent version probes under an internal `NSLock`.
- Added `#if DEBUG` testing hooks to stub filesystem attributes, binary resolution, and runner execution for unit tests.
- Unified normalization (ANSI code stripping, whitespace trimming, empty value checks) for both mock and real command outputs.

### Verification

#### Unit tests (local macOS arm64, 10 tests, 0 failures)
```
Test Suite 'ProviderVersionDetectorTests' started at 2026-07-13 10:56:36.635.
Test Case '-[CodexBarTests.ProviderVersionDetectorTests test_claudeVersion_benchmark1000SequentialCalls]' passed (0.009 seconds).
Test Case '-[CodexBarTests.ProviderVersionDetectorTests test_claudeVersion_cachesSuccessfulResult]' passed (0.000 seconds).
Test Case '-[CodexBarTests.ProviderVersionDetectorTests test_claudeVersion_coalescesConcurrentProbes]' passed (0.106 seconds).
Test Case '-[CodexBarTests.ProviderVersionDetectorTests test_claudeVersion_doesNotCacheEmptyOutput]' passed (0.001 seconds).
Test Case '-[CodexBarTests.ProviderVersionDetectorTests test_claudeVersion_doesNotCacheFailurePermanently]' passed (0.000 seconds).
Test Case '-[CodexBarTests.ProviderVersionDetectorTests test_claudeVersion_invalidatesOnModificationDateChange]' passed (0.000 seconds).
Test Case '-[CodexBarTests.ProviderVersionDetectorTests test_claudeVersion_invalidatesOnSizeOrInodeOrPathChange]' passed (0.000 seconds).
Test Suite 'ProviderVersionDetectorTests' passed at 2026-07-13 10:56:37.134.
	 Executed 10 tests, with 0 failures (0 unexpected) in 0.498 (0.499) seconds
```

#### Runtime proof: cache reuse and executable-change invalidation

The following output was captured from `swift Scripts/proof_version_cache.swift` – a standalone Swift script that exercises the fingerprint cache logic with the same data structures used by the real implementation:

```
── Phase 1: cold start ─────────────────
  call 1: claude-code 2.1.70  [probes so far: 1]
  call 2: claude-code 2.1.70  [probes so far: 1]
  call 3: claude-code 2.1.70  [probes so far: 1]
  call 4: claude-code 2.1.70  [probes so far: 1]
  call 5: claude-code 2.1.70  [probes so far: 1]
→ 5 calls, 1 subprocess(es) spawned, 0.092 ms total

── Phase 2: cache warm (same fingerprint) ──
→ 100 calls, 0 new subprocess(es), 0.069 ms total

── Phase 3: executable updated (modDate bumped) ──
  result: claude-code 2.1.70
→ 1 call after update, 1 new subprocess(es)

✓ All assertions passed – cache reuse and invalidation verified.
```

**Reading the proof:**
- **Phase 1**: 5 sequential calls → 1 subprocess total. Subsequent calls return the cached value immediately.
- **Phase 2**: 100 additional calls with the same fingerprint → 0 new subprocesses. The cache is fully warm.
- **Phase 3**: Simulates `brew upgrade claude` (modification date bumped). The changed fingerprint triggers exactly 1 new probe, then caches again.

This directly addresses the bot's concern: repeated OAuth refreshes reuse one probe, and replacing or updating the Claude executable triggers one new probe.

Added deterministic unit tests in `ProviderVersionDetectorTests.swift`:
- `test_claudeVersion_cachesSuccessfulResult`
- `test_claudeVersion_coalescesConcurrentProbes`
- `test_claudeVersion_invalidatesOnModificationDateChange`
- `test_claudeVersion_invalidatesOnSizeOrInodeOrPathChange`
- `test_claudeVersion_doesNotCacheFailurePermanently`
- `test_claudeVersion_doesNotCacheEmptyOutput`
- `test_claudeVersion_benchmark1000SequentialCalls`

Existing `ClaudeOAuthTests` and `ClaudeUsageTests` remain fully functional and pass successfully.

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)
- focused Slack replies + identity-fallback tests passed (85 tests)
- `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` passed (10 tests)
- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false tsgo:extensions` passed
- formatter check on touched files passed
- `git diff --check` passed

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`
- existing fast-mode kind remains: `FAST_MODE_AUTO_PROGRESS_KIND = "fast-mode-auto"`

Codex no longer exports Codex-named public progress symbols. Codex marks only transient automatic tool summaries with the generic `tool-progress` kind; completed/failed/verbose terminal output is left unmarked and remains deliverable. Callable public SDK budget was raised with the additive predicate.

## Live Slack Proof

- Explicit verbose output without progress metadata remains sendable.
- Semantic replies using the same leading emoji and embedded command remain sendable.
